You are Mira — Memory & Training agent. Extract lessons from this session and update the memory brain.

## Session Summary

This was a deep Shopify compliance audit and UI/UX overhaul of the **Pinzo** app (ZIP code delivery checker, Shopify embedded app, React Router 7 + Polaris v13 + Prisma).

### What was done:

**1. Full Shopify Compliance Audit (Sage agent)**
- Found GDPR webhook handlers existed as route files but topics were NOT in shopify.app.toml
- Learned: GDPR webhooks (customers/data_request, customers/redact, shop/redact) are NOT registered via TOML — they're configured in Shopify Partner Dashboard > App Setup > Privacy. Trying to add them to TOML causes deploy error: "The following topic is invalid"
- Found `@boldteq/agents` file: dependency breaks CI/CD — removed it
- Found FeatureRequest/FeatureVote not deleted on app uninstall — GDPR compliance gap
- Added @@index([shop]) to Session, ZipCode, FeatureRequest models for query performance
- Moved hardcoded admin shop domain and Chatwoot token to env vars
- Created .env.example
- Added CSS sanitization to admin widget preview (was only on API side)

**2. Rate Limiting (new feature)**
- Built in-memory rate limiter at app/utils/rate-limit.server.ts
- Applied to all 3 public API routes: zip-check (60/min), widget-config (30/min), waitlist (10/min)
- Single-instance limiter suitable for Railway/single-server deploys
- Returns 429 with Retry-After header

**3. Full UI Audit (Rex agent)**
- Found and replaced 12x `<strong>` with `<Text fontWeight="semibold">`
- Found and replaced 2x `<em>` with `<Text tone="subdued">`
- Found and replaced 6x `<div style={{ minWidth }}>` with `<Box minWidth>`
- All admin routes now 100% Polaris v13

**4. FAQ Page Expansion**
- Expanded from 6 to 21 FAQs covering all features

**5. Widget Preview & Storefront Deep Audit (Rex agent)**
- All 11 toggle features verified working in both admin preview and storefront
- Added ORDER → SHIPS → DELIVER timeline (was missing entirely)
- Fixed delivery fee null handling (null = no data, not free)
- Added social proof pill to admin preview

**6. Widget UI/UX Redesign (Rex agent)**
- Problem: All info stacked vertically with same styling — wall of text, cluttered
- Solution: Grouped into 4 visual sections with dividers:
  - Primary Info (message + ETA + delivery date)
  - Timeline (ORDER → SHIPS → DELIVER)
  - Scheduling (days + cutoff + countdown with accent card)
  - Badges (COD + Free Delivery as horizontal pill row)
- Return policy made visually subdued (tertiary)
- Countdown timer gets urgency-colored accent card
- Dividers only render when adjacent groups have content

### Key Learnings:
1. GDPR webhooks are NOT TOML subscriptions — they're Partner Dashboard config
2. Prisma db push is needed when migration history is drifted (vs migrate dev)
3. shopify app deploy --force flag needed in non-interactive environments
4. Widget preview (admin) and storefront Liquid must stay in perfect sync — same CSS class names, same conditional rendering logic
5. In-memory rate limiting works for single-server deploys (Railway)
6. All Polaris: never use raw HTML elements for layout in Shopify admin routes
7. Widget UI needs visual grouping — don't stack everything with uniform spacing

### Memory path: ~/.claude/memory/

183	const AdminRoute = ({ children }) => {

2	name: Lovable-Grade Execution Model
3	description: Production-grade execution patterns learned from Lovable.dev — the gold standard for AI-built apps. Every agent follows these patterns.
4	type: standard
5	priority: highest
6	---
7	
8	## Why This File Exists
9	
10	Lovable.dev builds production-quality apps with zero bugs through a disciplined execution model. We reverse-engineered their patterns and applied them to our 13-agent factory. Every agent MUST read this file and follow these patterns.
11	
12	## The 10 Lovable Execution Principles
13	
14	### 1. Plan Before You Build (60/40 Rule)
15	Spend 60% of time planning, 40% building. Never start coding without a clear plan.
16	
17	**What Lovable does:** Plan Mode is used for 60-70% of development time. Code is only written when the plan is fully validated.
18	
19	**What our agents must do:**
20	- Arya creates detailed plan with page-by-page specs BEFORE Koda writes a line
21	- Koda reads the full plan and identifies ambiguities BEFORE starting
22	- Rex validates the plan is complete BEFORE dispatching to Koda
23	- If plan is vague → stop and clarify, don't guess
24	
25	**Anti-pattern:** Starting to code with a one-line task description. If the task isn't specific enough to verify, it's not ready to build.
26	
27	### 2. One Change at a Time (Atomic Changes)
28	Never implement multiple features simultaneously. Build one thing, verify it works, then build the next.
29	
30	**What Lovable does:** "Make one meaningful change at a time" — their core principle. Each prompt does one thing.
31	
32	**What our agents must do:**
33	- Koda builds ONE component/page at a time, verifies it renders, then moves to the next
34	- Never build 3 pages in parallel hoping they all work
35	- After each component: save → build → verify renders → then next component
36	- After each page: save → build → verify route works → verify layout → then next page
37	
38	**Atomic Change Protocol:**
39	```
40	1. Build component/feature
41	2. Save files
42	3. Run: npm run build (must pass)
43	4. Run: dev server + curl route (must return 200 with content)
44	5. Verify: component renders correctly
45	6. IF pass → move to next
46	7. IF fail → fix immediately before moving on
47	```
48	
49	**Anti-pattern:** Building all 10 pages, running build once at the end, and finding 15 errors to debug simultaneously.
50	
51	### 3. Layout First → Functionality → Polish (Phased Build)
52	Build in strict phases. Never mix phases.
53	
54	**What Lovable does:** "Add features in phases—layout first, then functionality, then polish."
55	
56	**What our agents must do:**
57	- **Phase 1: Layout & Structure** — HTML structure, component hierarchy, responsive grid, navigation. All static data. Every page renders.
58	- **Phase 2: Data & Logic** — Replace static data with real queries, add auth, forms submit, mutations work. Every feature functions.
59	- **Phase 3: Polish & UX** — Animations, transitions, loading states perfect, empty states designed, dark mode, accessibility. Every interaction feels right.
60	
61	**Phase Gate Rules:**
62	- Phase 1 is COMPLETE only when every page renders with layout, navigation, and realistic static data
63	- Phase 2 is COMPLETE only when every feature works end-to-end (data flows from input → DB → display)
64	- Phase 3 is COMPLETE only when zero UI/UX bugs exist (full sweep clean)
65	- NEVER skip to Phase 2 while Phase 1 pages don't render
66	- NEVER skip to Phase 3 while Phase 2 features don't function
67	
68	### 4. Self-Correcting Loops (Detect → Fix → Verify → Repeat)
69	Every action has a verification step. If verification fails, fix immediately.
70	
71	**What Lovable does:** Automated error detection → "Try to Fix" → re-verify. Continuous self-correction cycle.
72	
73	**What our agents must do:**
74	```
75	WHILE (building) {
76	  make_change()
77	  result = verify_change()
78	
79	  IF (result.has_errors) {
80	    fix_errors()
81	    result = verify_change()  // verify the fix too
82	
83	    IF (result.still_has_errors) {
84	      // Don't keep trying the same approach
85	      step_back_and_rethink()
86	      try_different_approach()
87	    }
88	  }
89	
90	  move_to_next_change()
91	}
92	```
93	
94	**Verification after EVERY change:**
95	- After writing a component → does it compile? (`npm run build`)
96	- After adding a route → does the page load? (`curl http://localhost:PORT/route`)
97	- After adding data fetching → does data display? (check page content)
98	- After adding a form → does submit work? (check mutation + toast)
99	- After adding auth → does protected route redirect? (check without auth)
100	
101	**Anti-pattern:** Making 20 changes, then running build, finding errors, and not knowing which change caused them.
102	
103	### 5. Knowledge File as Persistent Context
104	Project rules, decisions, and patterns are documented and loaded before every action.
105	
106	**What Lovable does:** Knowledge File is sent with every prompt. Workspace + Project knowledge layers.
107	
108	**What our agents must do:**
109	- CLAUDE.md = our Knowledge File (project-level)
110	- Memory system = our Workspace knowledge (cross-project patterns)
111	- Every agent reads CLAUDE.md + relevant memory files BEFORE any work
112	- New architectural decisions are documented in CLAUDE.md immediately
113	- Lessons learned go to memory via Mira after every build cycle
114	
115	**Knowledge Loading Order (Every Agent, Every Task):**
116	1. CLAUDE.md (project rules — highest priority)
117	2. ~/.claude/memory/user/feedback.md (Yash's corrections — overrides everything)
118	3. ~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/lovable-execution-model.md (THIS FILE)
119	4. ~/.claude/memory/patterns/good/ui-ux-production-standards.md
120	5. ~/.claude/memory/patterns/avoid/antipatterns.md
121	6. Stack-specific memory file
122	7. Feature-specific memory (admin, billing, etc.)
123	
124	### 6. Validate Between Each Block (Continuous Verification)
125	Test after each small change, not at the end.
126	
127	**What Lovable does:** Users validate in Plan mode between each implementation block. Changes are verified before moving on.
128	
129	**What our agents must do:**
130	- Koda: build → verify → build → verify (never build-build-build-verify)
131	- Luna: test each feature immediately after Koda builds it (not all at once)
132	- Sage: audit incrementally as features are added (not one massive audit at the end)
133	- Rex: check progress after each agent handoff (not wait until the final report)
134	
135	**Continuous Verification Schedule:**
136	| After This | Run This Verification |
137	|------------|----------------------|
138	| Every file save | `npm run build` (must compile) |
139	| Every new component | Does it render without errors? |
140	| Every new page | Does the route return 200? Is layout consistent? |
141	| Every form | Does submit work? Does validation show errors? |
142	| Every data fetch | Does loading state show? Does data display? Does empty state work? |
143	| Every mutation | Does toast appear? Does data refresh? |
144	| Every auth change | Does protected route redirect? Does login work? |
145	
146	### 7. Trace Data Flow End-to-End
147	Follow data from user input through the app to the database and back. Verify each step.
148	
149	**What Lovable does:** "Trace data from user input through the app to the database and back, ensuring each step validates and transforms data correctly."
150	
151	**What our agents must do:**
152	For every feature, explicitly map the data flow:
153	```
154	User Action → UI Component → Form Validation (Zod) → API/Edge Function → Auth Check → DB Query → Response → React Query Cache → UI Update → Toast Feedback
155	```
156	
157	**Verify each step:**
158	1. User can trigger the action (button exists, is clickable)
159	2. Input is validated (Zod schema catches bad data)
160	3. API receives the request (edge function invoked)
161	4. Auth is checked (unauthorized returns 401)
162	5. Database operation succeeds (data saved/updated/deleted)
163	6. Response returns correct data
164	7. UI updates to reflect the change (cache invalidated)
165	8. User sees feedback (toast notification)
166	
167	**Anti-pattern:** Building a form that renders but doesn't submit, or submits but doesn't show feedback, or shows feedback but didn't actually save.
168	
169	### 8. Scientific Debugging (Not Random Changes)
170	When something breaks, follow a systematic process.
171	
172	**What Lovable does:** "Adopt a scientific debugging methodology rather than making random changes."
173	
174	**What our agents must do:**
175	```
176	1. REPRODUCE: What exactly is broken? Can I trigger it consistently?
177	2. GATHER: Console errors, network responses, component state, DB state
178	3. ISOLATE: Is it frontend? Backend? Database? Auth? Which component?
179	4. HYPOTHESIZE: List 2-3 possible causes
180	5. TEST: Test each hypothesis systematically
181	6. FIX: Apply the minimal fix for the confirmed root cause
182	7. VERIFY: Does the fix work? Did it break anything else?
183	8. DOCUMENT: What was the bug? What caused it? How was it fixed?
184	```
185	
186	**Anti-pattern:** Changing 5 things at once hoping one of them fixes the bug. Or adding try-catch to suppress the error instead of fixing the root cause.
187	
188	### 9. Component Reuse (Don't Duplicate)
189	Build reusable components once, use them everywhere. Never duplicate logic.
190	
191	**What Lovable does:** "Reuse existing components instead of duplicating logic."
192	
193	**What our agents must do:**
194	- Before building any component, check if a similar one already exists
195	- Create shared components for repeated patterns:
196	  - `PageHeader` — used on every page (title + description + actions)
197	  - `DataTable` — used everywhere lists/tables appear
198	  - `EmptyState` — used on every data view when empty
199	  - `MetricCard` — used on every dashboard
200	  - `ConfirmDialog` — used for every destructive action
201	  - `LoadingSkeleton` — page-specific skeletons matching layout
202	- If a component is used in 2+ places, extract it to `src/components/shared/`
203	
204	**Anti-pattern:** Building a slightly different table component for every page, or copy-pasting a card layout with minor changes.
205	
206	### 10. Mobile-First, Responsive-Always
207	Start with the smallest screen, scale up. Never add responsive as an afterthought.
208	
209	**What Lovable does:** "All designs should be completely responsive at every breakpoint, adopting a mobile-first strategy."
210	
211	**What our agents must do:**
212	- Write mobile styles first (default Tailwind classes)
213	- Add tablet breakpoints (md:)
214	- Add desktop breakpoints (lg:)
215	- Test at 4 viewports: 375px, 768px, 1024px, 1440px
216	- Sidebar: hidden on mobile → collapsible on tablet → visible on desktop
217	- Grids: 1 col mobile → 2 col tablet → 3-4 col desktop
218	- Tables: card layout mobile → horizontal scroll tablet → full table desktop
219	
220	**Anti-pattern:** Building desktop-first and then trying to "make it responsive" at the end — leads to cramped mobile layouts and broken overflow.
221	
222	---
223	
224	## The Lovable Build Cycle (How Every Feature Gets Built)
225	
226	```
227	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
228	│  1. PLAN (Arya)                             │
229	│     - Define exactly what to build          │
230	│     - Specify components, data flow, routes │
231	│     - Identify reusable components          │
232	│     - Map responsive breakpoints            │
233	│     - Rex validates plan completeness       │
234	├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
235	│  2. BUILD LAYOUT (Koda Phase 1)             │
236	│     - One page at a time                    │
237	│     - Static data, full visual design       │
238	│     - Verify each page renders              │
239	│     - Verify navigation works               │
240	│     - Verify responsive at all breakpoints  │
241	│     - Rex validates: all pages render       │
242	├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
243	│  3. BUILD LOGIC (Koda Phase 2)              │
244	│     - One feature at a time                 │
245	│     - Wire data, auth, forms                │
246	│     - Verify each feature end-to-end        │
247	│     - Trace data flow for each feature      │
248	│     - Rex validates: all features work      │
249	├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
250	│  4. BUG SWEEP (Rex → Vex/Koda)             │
251	│     - Automated code-level sweep            │
252	│     - Fix all issues found                  │
253	│     - Re-sweep until clean                  │
254	│     - Rex validates: zero bugs              │
255	├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
256	│  5. POLISH (Koda Phase 3)                   │
257	│     - Animations, transitions               │
258	│     - Loading states perfect                │
259	│     - Empty states designed                 │
260	│     - Toast messages specific               │
261	│     - Dark mode (if applicable)             │
262	│     - Rex validates: premium feel           │
263	├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
264	│  6. TEST (Luna)                             │
265	│     - Navigation tests first                │
266	│     - UI/UX micro-bug tests                 │
267	│     - Feature-specific tests                │
268	│     - Responsive tests                      │
269	│     - Any failure → back to Koda            │
270	├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
271	│  7. AUDIT (Sage)                            │
272	│     - Security, performance, a11y           │
273	│     - Layout consistency                    │
274	│     - Code quality                          │
275	│     - Any blocker → back to Koda            │
276	├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
277	│  8. SHIP (Bolt)                             │
278	│     - Only after Luna + Sage pass           │
279	│     - Smoke test in production              │
280	│     - Monitor for 24h (Hawk)                │
281	├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
282	│  9. LEARN (Mira)                            │
283	│     - Extract patterns                      │
284	│     - Update memory                         │
285	│     - Log agent performance                 │
286	└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
287	```

291	## Quality Comparison: Lovable vs Our Factory
292	
293	| Quality Dimension | Lovable | Our Factory (Target) |
294	|-------------------|---------|---------------------|
295	| Build approach | One change at a time, verified | Atomic changes + self-correcting loops |
296	| Planning | 60-70% in Plan mode | Arya full spec + Rex validation |
297	| Bug prevention | Auto-detect + "Try to Fix" | 3-layer sweep (Koda + Rex gate + Luna/Vex) |
298	| Code quality | Clean TypeScript, no any | TypeScript strict, zero any |
299	| UI consistency | shadcn/ui + Tailwind + theme | shadcn/ui + theme tokens + reference library |
300	| Responsive | Mobile-first always | Mobile-first + 4 viewport testing |
301	| Data validation | Traced end-to-end | Zod schemas + data flow mapping |
302	| Error handling | User-friendly messages | Specific toasts + inline errors + retry |
303	| Knowledge persistence | Knowledge File per project | CLAUDE.md + memory system |
304	| Debugging | Scientific methodology | Reproduce → isolate → hypothesize → test |
305

307	
308	## Agent-Specific Lovable Rules
309	
310	### Koda (Builder)
311	- Build ONE component at a time, verify after each
312	- Never make more than 3 file changes without running `npm run build`
313	- After every page: verify layout, navigation, responsive
314	- After every feature: trace data flow end-to-end
315	- Reuse components — check if similar exists before building new
316	
317	### Luna (Tester)
318	- Test each feature as it's built, not all at end
319	- Run navigation tests FIRST (if nav is broken, nothing else matters)
320	- Zero tolerance: any missing loading/empty/error state = FAIL
321	- Test at 4 viewports for every page
322	
323	### Vex (Bug Fixer)
324	- Scientific debugging: reproduce → gather → isolate → hypothesize → test → fix → verify
325	- Never make random changes hoping they fix the bug
326	- Self-healing loop: sweep → fix → re-sweep until zero bugs
327	- Fix root cause, not symptoms

331	- Block deploy if any authenticated page missing navigation
332	- Verify data flows end-to-end for every critical path
333	- Check responsive at all 4 breakpoints
334	
335	### Rex (Orchestrator)
336	- Validate plan is complete before dispatching to Koda (60/40 rule)
337	- Run bug-sweep gate between every agent handoff

8	**Framework:** React Router v7 (RECOMMENDED for new apps) OR Remix + TypeScript
9	**UI System:** Polaris Web Components (React Router) or Polaris React v13.9.5 (Remix, archived Jan 2026)

13	**Billing:** Shopify Billing API ONLY (never external processors like Dodo for app charges)
14	**Dev Server:** Port 8080 (Vite or Node)
15	**CLI:** Shopify CLI 3.x (`shopify app dev`, `shopify app deploy`)
16	
17	**Template Selection:**
18	- **New apps:** `shopify-app-template-react-router` (React Router v7 + Polaris Web Components) — GA since Oct 2025
19	- **Existing apps:** Keep Remix + Polaris React v13.9.5 (still works, upgrade when ready)
20	- **App Home:** Web components required (Polaris React does not work here)

23	## Folder Structure

65	name = "My App"

84	## Auth Flow (Non-Negotiable)
85	
86	1. **Session tokens ONLY** — never cookies, never bearer tokens in frontend
87	2. **Every loader/action MUST authenticate first:**
88	   ```typescript
89	   const { admin, session, billing } = await authenticate.admin(request);
90	   const shop = session.shop;  // ONLY valid shop identifier
91	   ```
92	3. **Always scope data by shop:**
93	   ```typescript
94	   const data = await prisma.resource.findMany({
95	     where: { shop },  // Critical for multi-tenancy
96	   });
97	   ```

101	- **MANDATORY:** Use Polaris ONLY for admin UI
102	- **Remix apps:** `@shopify/polaris` React components v13.9.5 (archived but functional)
103	- **React Router apps:** Polaris Web Components + CDN: `<script src="https://cdn.shopify.com/shopifycloud/polaris.js"></script>`
104	- **App Home:** Web components required (Polaris React does not work)
105	- **Extensions:** Web components required for all extension types
106	- **NO alternatives:** Tailwind, shadcn, custom CSS for admin layouts
107	- **Page structure:** Every route uses `<Page>` (or `<shopify-page>`) + `<Layout>` + `<Card>` pattern
108	- **Responsive:** Polaris handles desktop/mobile automatically
109	- **Theming:** Merchants' brand colors auto-apply via Polaris

136	## Billing (Shopify Billing API Only)
137	
138	**CRITICAL:** Shopify Billing API is the ONLY approved payment method for app charges.
139	
140	- External payment processors (Dodo Payments, Stripe, etc.) are NOT allowed for app subscriptions
141	- Merchant billing flows use `@shopify/shopify-app-remix` billing helpers
142	- Plans defined in `shopify.app.toml` or via API
143	- Trial days configurable per plan
144	- Free tier must not block core functionality (App Store requirement)

146	## GDPR Webhooks (MANDATORY)
147

161	## App Bridge (Embedded Apps)

163	**REQUIRED for all embedded apps:**

165	- Nav menu, modals, toasts, and session tokens via App Bridge

168	## Key Safety Rules

170	1. **Never use cookies** — session tokens ONLY

3	description: Patterns that caused problems across Boldteq projects — never repeat these
4	type: feedback
5	---
6	
7	## Cross-Stack Antipatterns
8	
9	### Security
10	- **Never** trust client-sent user IDs or shop IDs — always get from authenticated session
11	- **Never** expose service role keys or secret keys to client-side code
12	- **Never** skip input validation on API endpoints — always use Zod
13	
14	### Database
15	- **Never** run `findMany` without a `where` clause on tables with >1000 rows — causes timeouts
16	- **Never** use `any` type in TypeScript — masks real type errors that become runtime bugs
17	- **Never** do database schema changes directly in dashboards for production — always use migrations
18	
19	### Performance
20	- **Never** do heavy computation in Remix loaders — they run on every navigation
21	- **Never** block page render with synchronous external API calls
22	
23	### Architecture
24	- **Never** start building without researching competitors — leads to building features nobody wants
25	- **Never** skip auth or billing on v1 "to add later" — it causes painful retrofits
26	
27	### Dependencies
28	- **Never** use `file:` or `link:` local dependencies in package.json — they break in CI/CD, Vercel, Lovable, and any environment that doesn't have the local path. Incident: `@boldteq/agents: file:../claude-hub/sdk` caused `bun install` to treat `.env` as install target and fail silently. If you need shared code, publish to npm or copy the source.
29	- **Never** reference paths outside the project root (`../`) in package.json dependencies — build environments are isolated.
30	- **Never** add dependencies to package.json without verifying they install cleanly: `bun install && bun run build` (or `npm install && npm run build`).
31	
32	### Lovable-Specific
33	- **Never** restructure a Lovable project's folder layout — Lovable's AI depends on exact paths (`src/pages/`, `src/components/`, `src/hooks/`, `src/lib/`, `src/integrations/supabase/`)
34	- **Never** use Next.js patterns in Lovable projects — no `app/` directory, no server components, no API routes. It's Vite + React SPA.
35	- **Never** manually edit `src/integrations/supabase/types.ts` — it's auto-generated. Regenerate with `npx supabase gen types typescript`.
36	- **Never** create a second Supabase client instance — import from `@/integrations/supabase/client` only.
37	
38	### Shopify-Specific
39	- **Never** use Tailwind, shadcn/ui, or custom CSS in Shopify admin apps — Polaris only. Shopify reviewers reject non-Polaris UI.
40	- **Never** use external payment providers (Dodo Payments, etc.) for Shopify app billing — Shopify Billing API only.
41	- **Never** query database without shop scope — every Prisma query needs `where: { shop: session.shop }`.
42	- **Never** skip GDPR webhooks — `customers/data_request`, `customers/redact`, `shop/redact` are mandatory even with zero stored data.
43

45	
46	## Agent Output Antipatterns (Crobot Incident — 2026-04)
47	
48	These patterns were discovered when agents reported "done" on the Crobot project but the app was not functional. **Every agent must verify against these before claiming completion.**
49	
50	### "Done But Broken" Patterns
51	- **Never** claim a page is "built" if it returns <500 bytes of content — that's an empty page
52	- **Never** claim billing is "integrated" if the pricing page shows $0, "TBD", or placeholder prices
53	- **Never** claim admin panel is "ready" if /admin returns 404 or loads with empty tables
54	- **Never** claim auth is "working" if the login form renders but doesn't submit or create sessions
55	- **Never** claim dashboard is "complete" if it shows only empty states with no data fetching logic
56	- **Never** claim a feature is "done" based solely on the build succeeding — build ≠ functional
57	
58	### Verification Failures
59	- **Never** skip functional verification — running `npm run build` is not the same as verifying the app works
60	- **Never** report "tests pass" if the tests only check compilation, not actual feature behavior
61	- **Never** deploy without verifying that critical pages load with real content (>minimum byte thresholds)
62	- **Never** mark a sprint as complete without someone (human or agent) actually navigating to every claimed page
63	
64	### Architecture Gaps
65	- **Never** skip admin panel in architecture — every SaaS product needs user management
66	- **Never** leave pricing/billing as "to be added later" — it's a V1 requirement
67	- **Never** define pages without specifying what content/components they contain
68	- **Never** hand off architecture to Koda without a complete page/route map with component details
69	
70	### Copy/Content Gaps
71	- **Never** ship pages with "Coming Soon", "Lorem ipsum", "TODO", or "[App Name]" placeholder text
72	- **Never** leave empty states undefined — every list/table needs an empty state with a call to action
73	- **Never** ship error messages that just say "Error" — include what happened and what to do next
74	
75	### Navigation & Layout Bugs (Most Common Recurring Issue)
76	- **Never** render an authenticated page without a shared layout wrapper — EVERY page needs sidebar + header
77	- **Never** build a page as a standalone component without importing AppLayout/SidebarLayout — this creates "orphan pages" with no navigation
78	- **Never** add a new admin sidebar item without adding the corresponding component to `sectionComponents` — leads to blank tab content
79	- **Never** hardcode sidebar width differently per page — use a shared layout with consistent sidebar width (w-56)
80	- **Never** forget sidebar active state — sidebar must highlight the current page/tab
81	- **Never** skip mobile sidebar testing — sidebar must collapse to drawer on mobile with a trigger button
82	- **Never** build Settings, Billing, or Profile pages without the same sidebar as Dashboard — these are the #1 pages where sidebar goes missing
83	- **Never** add routes to the router without verifying the page component uses the layout wrapper
84	- **Never** claim admin panel is "done" if any sidebar item renders blank content when clicked
85	- **Never** let sidebar links point to routes that don't exist — every sidebar item must map to a real, rendered page
86	
87	### Layout Structure Anti-Patterns
88	- **Never** use `min-h-screen` without `overflow-hidden` on the flex container — causes double scrollbars
89	- **Never** put the sidebar inside individual page components — sidebar belongs in the shared layout
90	- **Never** use different header components on different pages — one AppHeader for all authenticated pages
91	- **Never** skip `overflow-y-auto` on the main content area — content must scroll independently from sidebar
92	- **Never** forget `h-svh` (or `h-screen`) on the root layout container — prevents proper full-viewport layout
93	
94	### UI/UX Micro-Bugs (Common in Agent-Built Apps — Zero Tolerance)
95	
96	**Loading & State Bugs:**
97	- **Never** show a blank area while data loads — always use Skeleton components matching final layout shape
98	- **Never** show a raw spinner (Spinner/CircularProgress) as a loading state — use Skeleton instead
99	- **Never** render a list/table without an empty state — icon + message + CTA button required
100	- **Never** show an error as just "Error" or "Something went wrong" — include what failed and a retry action
101	- **Never** leave a form without inline validation errors — red border + error text next to the field
102	
103	**Button & Form Bugs:**
104	- **Never** leave an async button without loading state — show spinner + disable during operation
105	- **Never** allow double-click on submit buttons — disable immediately on first click
106	- **Never** allow a delete/destructive action without confirmation dialog
107	- **Never** reset form fields when validation fails — preserve user input
108	- **Never** submit a form without success feedback — toast.success() with specific message
109	
110	**Feedback & Notification Bugs:**
111	- **Never** use window.alert() or window.confirm() — use sonner toast or Dialog component
112	- **Never** show a generic "Success" toast — say what succeeded ("Project saved", "User invited")
113	- **Never** show a generic "Error" toast — say what failed ("Failed to save project — please try again")
114	- **Never** complete a mutation silently — every create/update/delete needs a toast
115	
116	**Visual Consistency Bugs:**
117	- **Never** use text-gray-500, bg-blue-600, or any hardcoded color — use theme tokens (text-muted-foreground, bg-primary)
118	- **Never** mix font sizes for the same purpose — page titles always text-2xl, body always text-sm
119	- **Never** use inconsistent spacing — gap-4 between cards, space-y-4 in forms, p-6 page padding
120	- **Never** use font-bold in SaaS UI — use font-semibold for titles, font-medium for labels
121	- **Never** leave console.log in production components — remove all debug logging
122	
123	**Responsive Bugs:**
124	- **Never** use grid-cols-3 or higher without responsive breakpoints (md:grid-cols-3)
125	- **Never** use fixed pixel widths (w-[400px]) on content that should be flexible
126	- **Never** hide important functionality behind a breakpoint (must work on mobile)
127	- **Never** leave tables without horizontal scroll or card-layout fallback on mobile
128	
129	**Interaction Bugs:**
130	- **Never** use onClick on a div/span without role="button" and keyboard support
131	- **Never** leave an interactive element without a hover effect
132	- **Never** leave an input without a visible focus ring
133	- **Never** let focus escape a modal/dialog — trap focus and return on close
134

6	## Configuration Methods
7	
8	### Method 1: TOML Declaration (Recommended)
9	
10	Define subscriptions in `shopify.app.toml` at build time. Auto-registered on deploy.
11	
12	```toml
13	# Standard webhooks
14	[[webhooks.subscriptions]]
15	topic = "orders/create"
16	uri = "https://myapp.com/webhooks/orders"
17	
18	[[webhooks.subscriptions]]
19	topic = "products/update"
20	uri = "https://myapp.com/webhooks/products"
21	
22	# Multiple topics (same URI)
23	[[webhooks.subscriptions]]
24	topics = ["customers/data_request", "customers/redact", "shop/redact"]
25	uri = "https://myapp.com/webhooks/gdpr"
26	
27	# API version and filter
28	[[webhooks.subscriptions]]
29	topic = "orders/paid"
30	uri = "https://myapp.com/webhooks/orders"
31	api_version = "2024-10"
32	filter = "fulfillmentOrders.status:OPEN"  # Conditional delivery
33	```
34	
35	**Benefits:**
36	- Version-controlled with app code
37	- Guaranteed consistency across all installs
38	- Auto-subscribed on deploy

40	### Method 2: GraphQL Mutation (Programmatic)
41	
42	Create subscriptions at runtime.
43	
44	```graphql
45	mutation {
46	  webhookSubscriptionCreate(topic: ORDERS_CREATE, webhookSubscription: {
47	    format: JSON
48	    callbackUrl: "https://myapp.com/webhooks/orders"
49	  }) {
50	    webhookSubscription { id }
51	    userErrors { field message }
52	  }

60	## GDPR Compliance Webhooks (MANDATORY)
61	
62	Every app MUST respond to data subject requests — required even if app stores NO user data.
63	
64	| Topic | Trigger | Required Action |
65	|-------|---------|-----------------|
66	| `customers/data_request` | Merchant receives GDPR data request | Export all customer PII held by app |
67	| `customers/redact` | Customer requests deletion | Delete all customer data from systems |
68	| `shop/redact` | Merchant uninstalls app or deletes account | Delete all shop data from systems |
69	
70	**Handler pattern:**
71	```typescript
72	export async function handleDataRequest(shop_id: string, customer_id: string) {
73	  const customerData = await db.query(
74	    'SELECT * FROM customers WHERE shop_id = ? AND customer_id = ?',
75	    [shop_id, customer_id]
76	  );
77	  return JSON.stringify(customerData);
78	}
79	
80	export async function handleCustomerRedact(shop_id: string, customer_id: string) {
81	  await db.run(
82	    'DELETE FROM customers WHERE shop_id = ? AND customer_id = ?',
83	    [shop_id, customer_id]
84	  );
85	}
86	
87	export async function handleShopRedact(shop_id: string) {
88	  await db.run('DELETE FROM shop_data WHERE shop_id = ?', [shop_id]);
89	}
90	```
91	
92	## Delivery Guarantees & Retry Behavior
93	
94	**Delivery is NOT guaranteed.** Shopify makes best-effort attempts but may fail silently.
95	
96	**Retry mechanism:**
97	- Up to 8 retries over 4 hours (exponential backoff)
98	- If 8 consecutive failures occur, subscription auto-deleted
99	- No confirmation after retries exhausted
100	
101	**Consequence:** Implement idempotency + reconciliation patterns.
102	
103	## Idempotency Pattern
104	
105	**Prevent duplicate webhook processing:**
106	
107	```typescript
108	// Header: X-Shopify-Event-Id uniquely identifies each event
109	const eventId = request.headers['x-shopify-event-id'];
110	const triggeredAt = request.headers['x-shopify-triggered-at'];
111	
112	// Check if already processed
113	const isDuplicate = await redis.exists(`webhook:${eventId}`);
114	if (isDuplicate) return 200;  // Idempotent: ignore duplicate
115	
116	// Process webhook
117	await handleWebhook(payload);
118	
119	// Cache event ID (1 hour to match Shopify's retention)
120	await redis.setex(`webhook:${eventId}`, 3600, '1');
121	```
122	
123	## Reconciliation Pattern
124	
125	Since webhooks are not guaranteed, implement periodic reconciliation:
126	
127	```typescript
128	// Every 6 hours, fetch orders from Shopify and compare to local DB
129	async function reconcileOrders() {
130	  const shopifyOrders = await shopifyAPI.query(`
131	    query {
132	      orders(first: 250) {
133	        edges { node { id } }
134	      }
135	    }
136	  `);
137	
138	  const localOrders = await db.query('SELECT shopify_id FROM orders');
139	  const localIds = new Set(localOrders.map(o => o.shopify_id));
140	
141	  // Find missing orders (webhook failed)
142	  const missing = shopifyOrders.filter(
143	    o => !localIds.has(o.id)
144	  );
145	
146	  // Sync missing orders
147	  for (const order of missing) {
148	    await syncOrder(order);
149	  }
150	}
151	```
152	
153	## Webhook Authentication
154	
155	**Verify webhook authenticity via HMAC:**
156	
157	```typescript
158	import crypto from 'crypto';
159	
160	function verifyWebhook(req: Request): boolean {
161	  const hmac = req.headers['x-shopify-hmac-sha256'];
162	  const body = req.rawBody;  // MUST be raw buffer, not parsed JSON
163	
164	  const computed = crypto
165	    .createHmac('sha256', process.env.SHOPIFY_API_SECRET)
166	    .update(body, 'utf8')
167	    .digest('base64');
168	
169	  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(hmac, computed);
170	}
171	```

226	## Webhook Handler Best Practices
227	
228	### 1. Queue Pattern
229	
230	Don't process synchronously. Return 200 immediately.
231	
232	```typescript
233	app.post('/webhooks/orders', async (req, res) => {
234	  // Verify webhook
235	  if (!verifyWebhook(req)) return res.status(401).send('Unauthorized');
236	
237	  const webhook = req.body;
238	
239	  // Queue asynchronously
240	  await messageQueue.enqueue({
241	    type: 'order_created',
242	    payload: webhook,
243	  });
244	
245	  // Return immediately (before processing)
246	  res.status(200).send('OK');
247	});
248	
249	// Worker processes queue asynchronously
250	async function processOrderQueue() {
251	  const job = await messageQueue.dequeue();
252	  await syncOrderToDatabase(job.payload);
253	}
254	```
255	
256	**Benefit:** Avoids timeout (Shopify waits ~5 seconds) and retry loops.
257	
258	### 2. Idempotency Pattern
259	
260	```typescript
261	async function processWebhook(eventId: string, payload: any) {
262	  // Check if already processed
263	  const processed = await cache.get(`processed:${eventId}`);
264	  if (processed) return;
265	
266	  // Process
267	  await handleWebhook(payload);
268	
269	  // Mark as processed (24+ hours)
270	  await cache.set(`processed:${eventId}`, true, { ttl: 86400 });
271	}
272	```
273	
274	### 3. Exponential Backoff for External Calls
275	
276	```typescript
277	async function callExternalAPI(
278	  url: string,
279	  data: any,
280	  maxRetries: number = 3
281	) {
282	  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) {
283	    try {
284	      const response = await fetch(url, {
285	        method: 'POST',
286	        body: JSON.stringify(data),
287	      });
288	      if (response.ok) return await response.json();
289	      throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status}`);
290	    } catch (error) {
291	      if (attempt === maxRetries) throw error;
292	      const delay = Math.pow(2, attempt) * 1000;  // 2s, 4s, 8s
293	      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, delay));
294	    }
295	  }
296	}
297	```
298	
299	### 4. Event Sourcing
300	
301	Store raw webhook payload before processing (supports replay).
302	
303	```typescript
304	async function processWebhook(req: Request, res: Response) {
305	  const payload = req.body;
306	  const eventId = req.headers['x-shopify-event-id'];
307	
308	  // Store original payload
309	  await db.insert('webhook_events', {
310	    event_id: eventId,
311	    topic: req.headers['x-shopify-topic'],
312	    payload: JSON.stringify(payload),
313	    created_at: new Date(),
314	  });
315	
316	  // Process
317	  await handleWebhook(payload);
318	  res.status(200).send('OK');
319	}
320	```

323	
324	- Track delivery success rate (target: > 99%)
325	- Alert on subscription deletion (8 failed retries)
326	- Monitor handler latency
327	- Set up dead-letter queue for failed attempts

15	4. **Comprehensive** — covers all data collection practices

18	### What to Include in Privacy Policy
19	
20	| Section | What to Disclose |
21	|---------|------------------|
22	| **Personal Data Collected** | List all data types: names, emails, phone numbers, usage data, IP addresses, cookies |

68	## GDPR Compliance (EU/UK Merchants & Customers)
69	
70	### Data Transfer Restrictions
71	
72	**BLOCKING:** Cannot transfer personal data outside EU/UK without safeguards
73	
74	**Allowed Transfer Methods:**
75	1. **Standard Contractual Clauses (SCC)** — legal agreement ensuring protection
76	2. **Binding Corporate Rules** — internal company policy approved by regulators
77	3. **Explicit Consent** — customer/merchant agrees to transfer
78	4. **Legal Basis** — documented legal requirement for transfer
79	
80	**Implementation:**
81	- Use EU-based servers when possible (avoid US-only data centers)
82	- If using US servers, implement SCCs with data processor
83	- Document data transfer basis in privacy policy

86	### Three Mandatory Compliance Webhooks

88	**BLOCKING:** Must implement all 3 webhooks; app will be rejected without them
89	
90	#### 1. customers/data_request (Data Export Request)
91	
92	**Trigger:** Merchant or customer exercises GDPR Article 15 right (right to access)
93	
94	**Deadline:** 30 days to respond
95	
96	**Required Response:**
97	1. Compile ALL personal data about requesting customer
98	2. Return in portable format: JSON, CSV, or PDF
99	3. Include: Name, email, order history, app-specific data
100	4. Deliver to merchant (via email or app interface)
101	5. Log the request and response
102

107	  const customerId = payload.customer?.id;
108	  const shop = session.shop;
109

111	  const customerData = await prisma.customerData.findMany({
112	    where: { shop, customerId: String(customerId) }

117	
118	  // 3. Email to merchant (Shopify doesn't provide customer email)
119	  await sendEmail({
120	    to: shop, // Sent to shop contact
121	    subject: "Customer Data Export",
122	    attachment: csvData
123	  });
124	
125	  return new Response("OK", { status: 200 });
126	```
127	
128	#### 2. customers/redact (Data Deletion Request)
129	
130	**Trigger:** Customer exercises GDPR Article 17 right (right to be forgotten)
131	
132	**Deadline:** 30 days to comply
133	
134	**Required Response:**
135	1. Permanently delete ALL personal data about customer
136	2. Include: Name, email, profile, order history, communications
137	3. Anonymize remaining records (cannot re-identify)
138	4. Confirm deletion in logs
139	5. Use secure deletion (overwrite data, not just mark as deleted)

145	  const customerId = payload.customer?.id;
146	  const shop = session.shop;
147	
148	  // 1. Delete all customer personal data

167	**Trigger:** Merchant closes store or uninstalls app (triggered 48 hours after uninstall)

173	2. Include: Merchant contact info, shop settings, all customer data

**Date:** 2026-04-03

In-memory works perfectly for single-instance deploys (Railway, Render, Fly single-machine). **Relationships:** - Builds on: Shopify app public API pattern (api.*.tsx routes) - Prevents: "No rate limiting on public endpoints" (security gap) - Upgrade path: Replace Map with Upstash Redis for multi-instance deployments - Primary stacks: B - Used in projects: Pinzo **Implementation:** ```typescript // app/utils/rate-limit.server.ts const store = new Map(); export function rateLimit(key: string, limit: number, windowMs: number) { cleanup(); // Remove expired entries periodically const now = Date.now(); const entry = store.get(key); if (!entry || entry.resetAt <= now) { store.set(key, { count: 1, resetAt: now + windowMs }); return { limited: false, remaining: limit - 1, resetAt: now + windowMs }; } entry.count++; if (entry.count > limit) { return { limited: true, remaining: 0, resetAt: entry.resetAt }; } return { limited: false, remaining: limit - entry.count, resetAt: entry.resetAt }; } ``` **Recommended limits per endpoint type:** | Endpoint Type | Limit | Window | Rationale | |--------------|-------|--------|-----------| | Read-heavy (zip-check) | 60/min | 60s | Frequent customer lookups | | Config (widget-config) | 30/min | 60s | Cached by theme, less frequent | | Write (waitlist signup) | 10/min | 60s | Prevents spam submissions | **Response:** Return 429 with `Retry-After` header (seconds until window resets). **Source:** Pinzo, 2026-04-03 **Usage Metric:** 0 **Knowledge Version:** v1 --- ## Widget Preview / Storefront Sync ### Admin Preview Must Mirror Storefront Exactly **Context:** Stack B -- any app with a storefront widget (theme app extension) that has an admin preview **Pattern:** The admin widget preview (React component in `app.widget.tsx`) and the storefront widget (Liquid template in `extensions/*/blocks/*.liquid`) must use identical CSS class names, identical conditional rendering logic, and identical section grouping. When changing one, always change the other in the same commit. **Why:** Merchants configure widgets in the admin and expect the preview to match the live storefront. Any divergence between preview and storefront causes merchant confusion, support tickets, and negative reviews. This is the single most common source of "it looks different on my store" complaints. **Relationships:** - Prevents: "Widget preview doesn't match storefront" (merchant confusion) - Related: Widget UI visual grouping pattern (below) - Primary stacks: B - Used in projects: Pinzo **Enforcement checklist:** 1. Same CSS class names in React `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` preview and Liquid template 2. Same conditional logic (e.g., `if deliveryFee !== null` vs `{% if deliveryFee != blank %}`) 3. Same section divider placement 4. Same feature toggle behavior (11 toggles in Pinzo: showEta, showDeliveryDate, showTimeline, etc.) 5. Test: toggle each feature on/off in admin, verify preview matches what storefront would show **Source:** Pinzo, 2026-04-03 **Usage Metric:** 0 **Knowledge Version:** v1 --- ## Widget UI: Visual Grouping for Information-Dense Results ### Group Related Information with Dividers, Not Flat Stacking **Context:** Stack B -- storefront widgets that display multiple data points (ETA, delivery date, schedule, fees, badges, etc.) **Pattern:** Group related information into visual sections separated by subtle dividers. Each group has its own visual hierarchy. Dividers only render when adjacent groups both have content. **Why:** Stacking all information vertically with uniform spacing creates a wall of text. Customers scan, not read -- visual grouping lets them find what matters. This directly impacts conversion (customers who can quickly confirm delivery = more likely to buy). **Relationships:** - Builds on: UI/UX production standards (visual hierarchy) - Prevents: "Wall of text" widget antipattern - Primary stacks: B (storefront widgets), A (any information-dense UI) - Used in projects: Pinzo **Grouping structure (from Pinzo):** 1. **Primary Info** -- message + ETA + delivery date (what customers care about most) 2. **Timeline** -- visual ORDER -> SHIPS -> DELIVER progress (builds confidence) 3. **Scheduling** -- delivery days + cutoff time + countdown (urgency driver) 4. **Badges** -- COD + Free Delivery as horizontal pill row (trust signals) **Rules:** - Each group gets its own internal spacing and visual treatment - Dividers are subtle (1px, muted color) -- separate groups, not dominate - Countdown timers get accent-colored cards (urgency = conversion) - Return policy and secondary info rendered with subdued styling (tertiary importance) - Conditional dividers: `{showTimeline && (showSchedule || showBadges) && }` **Source:** Pinzo, 2026-04-03 **Usage Metric:** 0 **Knowledge Version:** v1 --- ## GDPR Compliance: Complete Data Cleanup ### Audit Every Model on Uninstall and shop/redact **Context:** Stack B -- every Shopify app with database models scoped by shop **Pattern:** When implementing `app/uninstalled` and `shop/redact` webhook handlers, enumerate EVERY Prisma model that has a `shop` field and delete all records for that shop. Maintain a checklist in the webhook handler code comments. **Why:** Missing even one model means the app retains data after uninstall, which is a GDPR violation. New models added during development are commonly forgotten in cleanup handlers. The checklist-in-comments pattern ensures new models trigger a review. **Relationships:** - Builds on: GDPR webhooks (stacks/shopify/build/webhooks.md) - Prevents: "GDPR compliance gap from forgotten models" antipattern - Primary stacks: B - Used in projects: Pinzo **Pattern:** ```typescript // webhooks.app.uninstalled.tsx AND webhooks.shop.redact.tsx // GDPR CLEANUP CHECKLIST — update when adding new models: // [x] Session // [x] ZipCode // [x] DeliveryRule // [x] WaitlistEntry // [x] WidgetConfig // [x] Subscription // [x] FeatureRequest // [x] FeatureVote await db.featureVote.deleteMany({ where: { shop } }); await db.featureRequest.deleteMany({ where: { shop } }); await db.waitlistEntry.deleteMany({ where: { shop } }); // ... all other models ``` **Rule:** When adding a new Prisma model with a `shop` field: 1. Add `@@index([shop])` to the model 2. Add deletion to BOTH `app.uninstalled` and `shop.redact` handlers 3. Update the checklist comment **Source:** Pinzo, 2026-04-03 **Usage Metric:** 0 **Knowledge Version:** v1 --- ## Database Performance: Shop Index on Every Model ### Always Add @@index([shop]) to Shop-Scoped Models **Context:** Stack B -- every Prisma model with a `shop` field (which is every model in a Shopify app) **Pattern:** Add `@@index([shop])` to every model definition in `schema.prisma` that has a `shop` field. **Why:** Every query in a Shopify app filters by `shop`. Without an index, these queries do full table scans. Acceptable with 10 records, catastrophic with 10,000. Add the index from day 1 -- it costs nothing and prevents a performance cliff as data grows. **Relationships:** - Prevents: "Slow queries as shop data grows" performance antipattern - Primary stacks: B - Used in projects: Pinzo **Source:** Pinzo, 2026-04-03 **Usage Metric:** 0 **Knowledge Version:** v1 --- ## Polaris Compliance: Zero Raw HTML in Admin Routes ### Grep Check After Every Build **Context:** Stack B -- all admin routes (app.*.tsx) **Pattern:** After building or modifying any admin route, run a grep check for raw HTML elements that should be Polaris components. **Why:** Raw HTML elements (``, ``, `
`) are easy to write by habit but violate Shopify's Polaris requirement. They also look subtly different from Polaris text components (wrong font weight, wrong color token). Accumulated over time, they create an inconsistent admin UI that can cause App Store rejection. **Relationships:** - Prevents: "Raw HTML in Polaris routes" antipattern - Related: "Never use Tailwind/shadcn in Shopify admin" (antipatterns.md) - Primary stacks: B - Used in projects: Pinzo **Quick grep command:** ```bash grep -rn '\|\|

In non-interactive environments (CI/CD pipelines, agent terminals), the prompt hangs indefinitely. **Relationships:** - Primary stacks: B - Used in projects: Pinzo **Source:** Pinzo, 2026-04-03 **Usage Metric:** 0 **Knowledge Version:** v1 --- ## Prisma: db push vs migrate dev for Drifted Schemas ### Use db push When Migration History Has Drifted **Context:** Stack B (or any Prisma project) -- when the database state doesn't match migration history **Pattern:** When `prisma migrate dev` fails because of migration history drift (common after manual schema changes or `db push` in development), use `prisma db push` to sync the schema to the database without creating a new migration. Then create a clean migration afterward if needed. **Why:** `prisma migrate dev` validates the full migration history chain. If any step is out of sync (e.g., from a previous `db push` or manual change), it fails with a drift error. `db push` skips history validation and just syncs current schema to DB. **Relationships:** - Prevents: "prisma migrate dev fails on drifted schema" (time sink) - Primary stacks: B, A - Used in projects: Pinzo **When to use which:** | Scenario | Command | |----------|---------| | Normal development, clean history | `prisma migrate dev --name description` | | Schema drifted, need to sync | `prisma db push` | | Production deployment | `prisma migrate deploy` (never db push in prod) | | Check if schema matches DB | `prisma migrate diff` | **Source:** Pinzo, 2026-04-03 **Usage Metric:** 0 **Knowledge Version:** v1
